problem: Learning effective ranking models from sparse and incomplete human feedback with rigid assumptions about the ranking model and censoring mechanism is challenging.
approach: Introduces PIRATE algorithm that unifies existing frameworks by considering ranking models satisfying complete consensus property and a new positional censoring feedback model that generalizes winner and top-h feedback.
contribution: Provides near-optimal instance-dependent sample complexity bounds for learning from incomplete rankings under this general framework.

problem: Generative models should give credit to works they depend on, but current approaches lack formal mechanisms to ensure this attribution.
approach: Studies counterfactual credit attribution (CCA) in autoregressive models that give credit to deployment-time datasets, uncovering fundamental barriers to two natural approaches: CCA does not compose autoregressively and retrofitting requires exponential query complexity.
contribution: Establishes theoretical barriers showing CCA autoregressive models face significant challenges unlike differential privacy approaches.

problem: Extending multimodal LLMs to dense prediction tasks like segmentation and depth estimation typically requires task-specific decoders that complicate the model architecture.
approach: Proposes DenseMLLM which uses vision token supervision strategy for multiple labels and tasks to enable standard MLLMs to perform dense predictions without additional task-specific decoders.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance on dense prediction and vision-language benchmarks using a minimalist design with no architectural specialization.

problem: Diffusion language models require heuristic token unmasking strategies that need manual tuning and degrade with larger block sizes during inference.
approach: Formalizes masked diffusion sampling as an MDP and trains a single-layer transformer policy using reinforcement learning to map token confidences to unmasking decisions.
contribution: Trained policies match state-of-the-art heuristics in semi-autoregressive generation and outperform them in full-diffusion setting.

problem: Safety evaluation datasets lack geographic and cultural diversity, making it unclear whether cultural differences in safety ratings persist after controlling for demographics.
approach: Conducts multilevel modeling meta-analysis of safety datasets using Inglehart-Welzel cultural dimensions to jointly analyze geo-cultural and demographic correlates.
contribution: Demonstrates cultural zone membership explains variance in safety ratings beyond demographics (p<0.05 across 6 datasets) with ~10% of items being culturally sensitive.

problem: Video virtual try-on models fail to handle interactive scenarios where subjects actively engage with clothing through deformation and manipulation.
approach: Introduces iTryOn framework using video diffusion Transformer with multi-level interaction injection: 3D hand priors for spatial guidance and action-aware captions with rotational position embeddings for semantic guidance.
contribution: Enables video virtual try-on for interactive scenarios with active human-garment interactions like pulling or unzipping.

problem: LLM agents lose logical integrity over extended reasoning horizons because memory preprocessing compresses sequential dependencies into pre-defined structures that sever narrative coherence.
approach: Proposes E-mem framework shifting from memory preprocessing to episodic context reconstruction using heterogeneous hierarchical architecture where assistant agents maintain uncompressed contexts and master agent orchestrates planning.
contribution: Achieves 54% F1 on LoCoMo benchmark surpassing GAM by 7.75% while reducing token cost by 70%.

problem: Stochastic optimal control via dynamic programming suffers from error accumulation across time steps that remains theoretically underexplored.
approach: Formulates SOC in dynamic programming framework using RKHS-based value function estimation with Monte Carlo subsampling and derives error decomposition with backward time propagation analysis.
contribution: Provides theoretical error propagation analysis from maturity to initial stage with application to American option pricing.

problem: Multimodal fusion object detection suffers from substantial modality gap at the same backbone stage, making predefined stage-aligned fusion insufficient.
approach: Proposes MFH-NAS hybrid framework combining differentiable search for local fusion primitives with evolutionary search for global fusion topologies to discover optimal cross-stage connections.
contribution: Improves mAP@0.5 from 85.3% to 88.2% over strong fixed-stage fusion methods across LLVIP, RGBT-Tiny, and M3FD benchmarks.

problem: Reward design in RL remains challenging because hand-crafted rewards are hard to specify and learned rewards from preferences suffer from inefficiency and training instability.
approach: Proposes CoRe framework decomposing rewards into Formal Rewards (hand-designed based on task knowledge) and Residual Rewards (learned from video preferences) using vision-language models for feedback.
contribution: Outperforms existing approaches on ten robotic manipulation tasks in simulation and five real-world tasks through preference-aligned reward construction.

problem: Diffusion models for image restoration have high computational overhead when operating in pixel space or require repeated encoder-decoder inference in latent space.
approach: Proposes projecting data into lower-dimensional subspaces using dynamic resolution DMs to accelerate inference while adapting existing pixel-space methods DPS and DAPS into SubDPS and SubDAPS variants.
contribution: SubDAPS++ outperforms recent DM-based approaches in majority of scenarios with improved inference speed and reconstruction quality.

problem: Disease screening models for medical images lack interpretability and effective mechanisms to reference historical cases for transparent reasoning.
approach: Introduces EviScreen framework leveraging region-level evidence from historical cases through dual knowledge banks with evidence-aware reasoning module and contrastive retrieval for abnormality localization.
contribution: Achieves superior performance on disease screening benchmarks with enhanced interpretability through regional evidence retrieval and abnormality mapping.

problem: Speculative Jacobi Decoding suffers from token ambiguity during token verification because vision tokens correspond to local unclear details that cannot be accurately expressed by single tokens.
approach: Proposes SJD-SV that leverages token correlations to recognize semantic-aware token subsequences and performs verification at subsequence level rather than token-by-token.
contribution: Plug-in method achieving significant performance improvement when integrated into existing SJD variants for accelerating autoregressive image generation.

problem: Success conditioning as a policy improvement technique lacks theoretical understanding of what optimization problem it solves and when it provably succeeds.
approach: Proves success conditioning exactly solves a trust-region optimization problem maximizing policy improvement subject to chi-squared divergence constraint, where action-influence measures how random action variation affects success.
contribution: Shows success conditioning is conservative improvement operator that cannot degrade performance, with identity between relative improvement, policy change magnitude, and action-influence at every state.

problem: On-policy reinforcement learning methods like GRPO suffer from mode collapse where solutions concentrate on a single high-reward trajectory and cease exploring alternatives.
approach: Proposes DMPO (Distribution-Matching Policy Optimization) preventing mode collapse through forward KL minimization by constructing group-level target distribution and aligning policy to it.
contribution: Achieves 43.9% Quality Ratio on text-based NP-Bench (vs GRPO's 40.1%) and 43.1% on vision-based NP-Bench (vs 38.4%) with 9% and 12% improvements demonstrating diversity-preserving benefits.

problem: Multi-task instruct-tuning of LLMs suffers from cross-task interference where conflicting gradients on shared parameters degrade performance despite parameter isolation attempts.
approach: Proposes BADIT that decomposes LLM parameters into orthogonal high-singular-value LoRA experts representing basic abilities and dynamically enforces orthogonality via spherical clustering of rank-1 components.
contribution: Outperforms SOTA methods on SuperNI benchmark across 6 LLMs by better mitigating cross-task interference through orthogonal ability decomposition.

problem: LLM unlearning via knowledge deletion suffers from biased deletion that only suppresses token sequences without complete removal, while refusal-based approaches keep underlying knowledge intact risking re-emergence.
approach: Proposes Distinguishable Deletion paradigm restricting response distribution in latent representation rather than specific tokens, combined with Energy-based Unlearning Alignment using energy index to quantify knowledge presence.
contribution: Significantly outperforms previous methods by enabling complete knowledge erasure while distinguishing unlearned from retained content through energy-boundary enforcement.

problem: In low-resource settings where data cannot be pooled and verification uses only fragmented local samples, data selection becomes biased and accelerates model collapse during recursive synthetic-data training.
approach: Theoretically proves siloed selection accelerates collapse and induces power-law diversity decay, then constructs Wasserstein proxy references from multiple silos without sharing raw data.
contribution: Demonstrates collaborative proxy references mitigate diversity degradation better than local-reference selection on skewed distributions.

problem: Standard SGD convergence guarantees degrade on heavy-tailed data where gradients lack finite second moments, even though empirical moments are finite once data is fixed.
approach: Separates data sampling from optimization randomness showing heavy-tailed data induce dataset-dependent noise scaling as N^(2/alpha-1) under tail index alpha, then proves SGD with gradient clipping avoids this growth.
contribution: Provides finite-sum convergence guarantees for SGD with clipping under heavy-tailed data and derives generalization bounds showing tail behavior at population minimizer links optimization and generalization.

problem: Large language models lack capability to handle time-series data natively despite strong performance on multimodal data, limiting their application to medical reasoning with longitudinal and wearable data.
approach: Proposes OpenTSLM family of time series language models integrating time-series as native modality into pretrained LLMs via soft prompting or cross-attention, with three new time-series reasoning datasets.
contribution: Achieves F1 scores of 69.88% in sleep staging and 67.64% in HAR, with cardiologist evaluations confirming strong reasoning on raw ECG data.

problem: Quantization error reconstruction methods allocate entire rank budget to error reconstruction, which is suboptimal when weights have intrinsic low-rank structure that quantization corrupts.
approach: Proposes Structured Residual Reconstruction (SRR) that preserves top-k singular subspace before quantization, quantizes only residual, and uses remaining rank for error reconstruction with theory-guided criterion.
contribution: Achieves consistent perplexity reductions across diverse models with 5.9 percentage-point average gain on GLUE under 2-bit QPEFT.

problem: Video creation systems treat script drafting and key-shot design as disjoint tasks using separate models, limiting narrative coherence and director-like creative control.
approach: Proposes UniMAGE unified director model using Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that unifies text and image generation with interleaved concept learning followed by disentangled expert learning.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance among open-source models generating logically coherent scripts and visually consistent keyframes.

problem: Soft label supervision from teacher models for dataset distillation causes local semantic drift when using limited crops per image, as visually ambiguous crops deviate from image-level ground-truth semantics.
approach: Proposes HALD that uses hard labels as content-invariant semantic anchors hybridized with soft labels to calibrate drift, providing intermediate corrective signals while preserving fine-grained soft label benefits.
contribution: Achieves 42.7% ImageNet-1K accuracy with only 285M soft-label storage (100x reduction) outperforming LPLD by 9.0%.

problem: Masked autoregressive models for text-to-image generation weaken spatial topology by flattening 2D latents into 1D sequences, limiting precise layout alignment for instance-level control.
approach: Proposes StructMAR integrating 2D Rotary Positional Embeddings with Layout-Guided Attention Bias to explicitly bias latent tokens toward layout instances, plus GRPO refinement to align MAR objective with detector-based metrics.
contribution: Achieves 57.2 AP on COCO-Position and 79.4 mIoU, 61.7 ISR on COCO-MIG with 4.05x inference speedup.

problem: Understanding how parameter symmetries relate to neural network phenomena like linear mode connectivity requires clarifying the exact interplay between parameters, data, and learned representations.
approach: Develops theoretical framework of effective function classes (functions a neuron can realize with their norm cost) and formalizes effective symmetry breaking via neuron identifiability across independent training runs.
contribution: Shows neural networks admit large families of approximately equivalent solutions even in structurally asymmetric models and characterizes when representation merging without alignment admits linear low-loss paths.

problem: One-step prediction of unknown marginally stable nonlinear dynamical systems is challenging without understanding how to learn effective mappings from observations.
approach: Describes algorithm based on spectral filtering using spectral representation of systems with online convex optimization for vanishing prediction error on nonexpansive systems.
contribution: Provides theory for spectral filtering on linear dynamical systems incorporating noise correction and asymmetric dynamics with rates governed by control-theoretic notion of learnability.

problem: 3D shape classification methods overlook geometric-topological regularities and symmetry principles intrinsic to CAD boundary representations.
approach: Introduces EquiCAD framework integrating equivariant representations with graph-based reasoning by leveraging group-theoretic decomposition of curve and surface descriptors with hierarchical message passing.
contribution: Achieves substantial improvements on SolidLetters, Parts, Machining Feature benchmark, and newly constructed Features dataset over prior state-of-the-art.

problem: High-fidelity point cloud completion and generation rely on long sampling schedules creating substantial inference latency without distillation or rectification trade-offs.
approach: Presents 3D MeanFlow performing one-step average-velocity transport with instantaneous-average consistency objective and shape-level constraint, plus PointPlug for integrating completion into 3D object detectors.
contribution: Achieves one-step sampling with order-of-magnitude speedup while maintaining competitive fidelity, improving evaluated detectors on nuScenes and KITTI.

problem: Existing safety steering methods for defending against jailbreak prompts are supervised and tied to static training sets, failing on unseen out-of-distribution attacks.
approach: Proposes zero-shot defense using unsupervised latent direction discovery to simulate jailbroken activations without knowing jailbreak strategy, combined with bi-level adversarial training steering these states to refusal regions.
contribution: Achieves strong defense with attack success rates mostly below 5% across three LLMs and six classical jailbreak families.

problem: Verifying ensemble properties like robustness or fairness in decision tree ensembles is NP-hard with most research targeting specific verification tasks rather than unified approaches.
approach: Explores ensemble verification through OC-space (set of all possible output combinations) providing unifying view where variety of verification tasks become simple searches answered in linear or quadratic time.
contribution: Shows generic OC-space approach can be faster than task-specific approaches while being flexible for diverse verification objectives.

problem: Integrated Gradients for feature attribution yields unreliable explanations when integration path passes through regions with noisy gradients outside the data manifold.
approach: Proposes Manifold-Aligned Guided Integrated Gradients (MA-GIG) constructing attribution paths in latent space of VAE and decoding intermediate states to bias path toward learned generative manifold.
contribution: Produces faithful explanations by aggregating gradients on path features proximal to input, reducing off-manifold noise and outperforming prior path-based attribution methods.

problem: Time series imputation methods re-discover feature relationships at each layer lacking persistent anchors to maintain consistent representations across network depth.
approach: Proposes HELIX assigning learnable feature identity (persistent embedding) to each feature capturing intrinsic semantic properties throughout network with hybrid temporal-feature attention.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance surpassing 16 baselines on 5 public datasets across 21 experimental settings with learned identities aligning to latent physical and semantic structure.

problem: Object reassembly task in n-dimensional space is invariant to global rigid motions, but training on SE(n)^N is ill-posed because losses penalize different global transforms as distinct.
approach: Proposes SE(n)-invariant framework with Global Gauge Fixing strategy and quotient-invariant Flow Matching objective via orthogonal projection onto horizontal tangent bundle.
contribution: Improves accuracy on polygonal jigsaw puzzles and 3D fracture reassembly benchmarks through construction that factors out global pose at each timestep.

problem: LLM-based formal verification lacks concrete behavioral feedback and treats proof generation as static end-to-end prediction tied to limited training datasets.
approach: Presents ExVerus counterexample-guided framework enabling LLMs to reason about proofs using behavioral feedback via counterexamples and generalize them into inductive invariants.
contribution: Significantly improves proof accuracy, robustness, and token efficiency over state-of-the-art prompting-based Verus proof generator.

problem: Causal language models factorizing sequences using only preceding context leave future information unexploited during training despite its availability.
approach: Introduces Regret Pre-training framework grounded in LUPI paradigm with dual-view architecture generating causal Student and future-conditioned Teacher distributions, transferring future-aware signals via regret loss.
contribution: Achieves 33.9% average accuracy with GlobalRegret and 32.2% with LocalRegret on nine tasks (vs baseline 30.2%), with 18.1 percentage point improvement on BoolQ.

problem: Genome language models fail to capture biological signal when using sequence reconstruction tasks inspired by NLP despite their potential for understanding regulatory genomics.
approach: Introduces pretraining tasks predicting evolutionary rate composable with sequence reconstruction enabling controlled comparison of predicting sequence only, rate only, or both.
contribution: Models pretrained on both sequence and evolutionary rate outperform sequence-only training on biologically grounded benchmarks and variant effect prediction tasks.

problem: Comparing effectiveness of autonomous ML engineering agents is difficult because systems combine different techniques in varying configurations making unclear which components drive performance.
approach: Conducts over 4,000 controlled experiments systematically ablating architectural components with K-live benchmark of 25 active competitions providing contamination-free dynamic evaluation.
contribution: Finds iterative feedback contributes more than architectural complexity and multi-agent coordination can hurt as often as help, providing concrete guidance for practitioners.

problem: High-stakes agent verification for clinical diagnosis lacks domain knowledge and reliable calibration in existing verifiers.
approach: Establishes GLEAN framework compiling expert-curated protocols into trajectory-informed correctness signals via guideline-grounded evidence accumulation with Bayesian logistic regression calibration.
contribution: Surpasses best baseline by 12% in AUROC and 50% in Brier score reduction on agentic clinical diagnosis across three diseases.

problem: Mixture of Experts architectures have unexploited sparsity at tensor and neuron levels during post-training and inference that can improve efficiency.
approach: Proposes complete expert partition for post-training and threshold-based token-expert dropping for inference with dual-threshold approach and partial expert partition for enhanced trade-off.
contribution: Improves Mixtral-8x7B by 1% across nine benchmarks (4% on GSM8K) with 1.19x speedup and 0.5% accuracy gain when combining optimizations.

problem: KV cache eviction methods rely on instantaneous heuristic metrics assuming consistency across attention heads, overlooking heterogeneity in predictive fidelity and long-horizon utility.
approach: Proposes LU-KV formulating head-level budget allocation as global combinatorial optimization to maximize long-horizon marginal contribution using convex-hull relaxation and greedy solver.
contribution: Reduces KV cache by 80% with minimal performance degradation on LongBench and RULER benchmarks while decreasing latency and GPU memory.
